topic: Sharp identification of individual-weighted strict Pareto benefit under multivariate response-pattern selection in cluster-randomized trials via a positive-stratum joint completion-and-cross-world LP, with compatibility onset, attained dual-certified bounds, nonrectangularity and majority-threshold results.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite product-ordered multivariate outcome in an iid Bernoulli cluster-randomized trial, derive sharp attained bounds on the individual-weighted same-patient probability of strict Pareto benefit and polynomial-time min-cut algorithms returning extremal couplings and explanatory cuts.

source_refs.claim: This multivariate CRT framework compares sampled treated and control individuals, rather than the two potential outcomes of the same patient.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar fraction-benefiting formulas exploit a total order, whereas a product order contains incomparable states and turns the favorable set into a nonnested bipartite relation. Current multivariate CRT work instead studies between-patient wins, an identified functional of the arm laws that does not answer the same-patient cross-world question. The missing mathematical step is a relation-specific transport dual that yields both endpoint formulas and constructive causal sharpness certificates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit capacity formulas for both endpoints, attainment proofs using feasible joint-potential-outcome tables, and max-flow/min-cut algorithms whose primal outputs are extremal couplings and whose dual outputs certify sharpness.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its framing around complementary benefit-and-risk outcomes, interpretable multivariate causal summaries, and informative cluster sizes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CRTs collect multiple complementary outcomes -> existing global summaries have ambiguous causal interpretation and weighting -> distinguish same-patient Pareto benefit from between-patient wins -> sharply bound that benefit from randomized-arm marginals

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt support-constrained coupling duality to strict product order and specialize the finite dual to a capacitated bipartite network.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoints optimize mass assigned to a fixed relation over all couplings with prescribed marginals.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the potential-outcome-table formulation and feasible-table sharpness argument, replacing scalar triangular cells by a product-order relation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the scalar ordinal version of the same cross-world probability-of-benefit problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt optimal-transport dual scores and covariate-assisted inference for estimated marginal laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets are transport-dual partial-identification endpoints; the new problem adds cluster-level scores and tied cuts.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when strict Pareto-benefit capacity is point identified from two finite product-ordered arm marginals and when every compatible coupling implies, or rules out, majority benefit.

source_refs.claim: For scalar ordinal outcomes, the fraction benefiting is generally partially identified, with point identification under special support configurations.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

source_refs.claim: Monotone-coupling existence is equivalent to inequalities over increasing sets, suggesting cut conditions on finite posets.
source_refs.author: Volker Strassen

open_problems.why_unsolved: On a chain, cumulative thresholds and separated supports reduce identification to nested inequalities. On a product poset, incomparable state pairs create support rectangles on which strict dominance varies, so equality of the two transport extrema cannot be read from coordinatewise stochastic dominance or marginal win probabilities. Existing work does not supply necessary-and-sufficient support geometry for constancy of this relation across the transportation polytope.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Necessary-and-sufficient zero-pattern or support-rectangle conditions for equal endpoints, together with finite cut-inequality characterizations of guaranteed and impossible majority benefit and counterexamples to scalarization.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates the clinically interpretable fraction benefiting and isolates exceptional support configurations that collapse its identified set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects do not reveal how many patients benefit -> same-patient benefit is cross-world and usually partially identified -> support restrictions can collapse the scalar interval -> characterize collapse and majority certification for Pareto outcomes

method_exemplars.technique: Use increasing-set inequalities and constrained-coupling duality to translate constancy of the relation cost into cut equalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Point identification asks whether every coupling with the prescribed marginals assigns identical mass to one support relation.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize scalar support and stochastic-dominance arguments, replacing nested cumulative sets by antichains and rectangles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the exact scalar analogue of strict-benefit point identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt confidence-set construction for an identified fraction-benefiting interval to optimization over product-order support geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The inferential object is again a pair of endpoints for a same-patient benefit probability.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish simultaneous whole-identified-set inference for cross-fitted cluster-AIPW Pareto-capacity endpoints when several primal couplings or dual minimum cuts tie or exchange order under local perturbations.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cluster-AIPW can yield a joint Gaussian limit for arm-state probabilities, but each capacity endpoint is a piecewise-linear extremum over cuts. At a tie its derivative is itself an extremum over the active-cut set, so ordinary one-cut delta methods and naive bootstraps are nonuniform. The prior review also identifies an unresolved bridge from estimator-side rate assumptions to primitive learner classes. A resolution must therefore combine cluster empirical-process expansions with primitive cross-fitting rates and derivative-aware inference uniformly over exact ties and local cut switching.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint cluster-level limit theorem for both capacity estimators, an explicit directional derivative at arbitrary tied-cut laws, and a feasible multiplier or numerical-delta procedure with uniform simultaneous coverage of the entire interval.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its arc from a meaningful cross-world target through transport bounds to nuisance-assisted, coverage-valid inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Important causal targets depend on unobserved joint potential outcomes -> transport duality gives sharp observable-law bounds -> nuisance learning can improve precision but complicates validity -> obtain simultaneous cluster-robust inference at tied Pareto cuts

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and bootstrap the Hadamard directional derivative of the min/max-cut value map instead of bootstrapping the nonsmooth map directly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite min-cut value is polyhedral and directionally differentiable, with nondifferentiability exactly at tied optimal cuts.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt intersection-bound bias correction and active-inequality selection to simultaneous lower and upper cut envelopes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each endpoint is an extremum of finitely many affine cut scores.

source_refs.excerpt: every common score test induces the full-observation test ... with identical rejection probability

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditioning restricts feasible couplings stratum by stratum, while complete cluster records can reveal within-cluster state compositions and size-dependent mixtures. Standard covariate-assisted partial identification assumes iid units, and CRT efficiency theory distinguishes individual from cluster weighting without comparing cross-world transport sets. The prior experiment-comparison proof obtains equality because a score is a measurable reduction of the full observation; here that step must be replaced by conditions under which added conditional marginals leave every active cut capacity unchanged.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp interval-inclusion theorem with necessary-and-sufficient active-cut conditions for equality among pooled, baseline-stratified, and full-cluster regimes, plus finite-support witnesses for every strict inclusion and estimand-aligned limit theory.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes the analysis around the scientific estimand and explains why informative cluster size makes individual and cluster averages diverge.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CRT analyses must specify whose average is targeted -> informative sizes make common weightings answer different questions -> cross-world bounds can also change with the information level -> characterize pooled, stratified, and full-cluster Pareto regions

method_exemplars.technique: Use conditional optimal-transport duality and averaging of stratum-specific bound functions to compare pooled and refined regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired nesting result is a clustered finite-poset analogue of covariate-assisted tightening of cross-world bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt efficient CRT scores and explicit cluster-size weighting to conditional state probabilities while preserving the individual-average target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Informative size changes the patient-state mixture entering every cut score.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry cross-fitted clustered nuisance estimation and the individual-pair versus cluster-pair distinction to partial-identification endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest multivariate CRT treatment of efficient estimation with informative cluster sizes.

open_problems.open_problem: Under multivariate outcome missingness in a cluster-randomized trial, derive sharp observed-data Pareto-benefit bounds and doubly robust inference when joint arm-state laws are identified only under an explicit vector-valued restricted-MAR or sensitivity model.

source_refs.claim: The paper develops doubly robust CRT estimators for missing outcomes, covariates, and cluster-population sizes, plus sensitivity analysis for assumption violations.
source_refs.author: Bingkai Wang, Fan Li, and Rui Wang

source_refs.claim: PPACT randomized 106 provider clusters, measured several patient-reported and utilization outcomes, and reported 96% follow-up.
source_refs.author: Lynn DeBar, Meghan Mayhew, Lindsay Benes, et al.

source_refs.claim: Scalar fraction-benefiting intervals can be inferred without specifying cross-world association once relevant arm marginals and restrictions are available.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing doubly robust CRT missing-data methods target smooth means. Pareto benefit requires each arm's complete joint distribution over a multivariate state, and componentwise MAR or separate regressions need not identify complete-state probabilities under nonmonotone response patterns. Once state marginals are recovered, cross-world coupling remains partially identified and its transport endpoint is nonsmooth at tied cuts. The unresolved interface is the composition of within-arm joint-state recovery with cross-world Pareto transport.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Assumptions identifying or sharply bounding complete arm-state laws from incomplete CRT records, the induced sharp Pareto interval, and cross-fitted endpoint estimators with double robustness, simultaneous coverage, and a sensitivity parameterization when vector MAR fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination trial's clinical narrative, 106-cluster design, complementary outcomes, and incomplete-record context.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PPACT reports modest improvements on several outcomes but not opioid use -> an average composite cannot say how many patients improve jointly -> incomplete multivariate records complicate arm-state estimation -> obtain missingness-robust Pareto-benefit bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt scaled cluster weights, response and outcome nuisance models, cross-fitting, doubly robust scores, and tipping-point sensitivity analysis to every joint-state indicator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missingness and informative-size structure is the same, but the required first-stage parameter is a vector of complete-state probabilities.

method_exemplars.technique: Compose uncertainty regions for state laws with the optimal-transport dual rather than inserting point estimates before optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The observed-data identified set is a transport bound evaluated over uncertain nuisance laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply derivative-aware resampling to the outer min/max-cut map after doubly robust state-probability estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Tied optimal cuts make the endpoint map directionally but not fully differentiable.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing CRT randomization intervals invert tests for point-valued intervention effects, whereas Pareto benefit is a partially identified cross-world probability whose null constrains an entire coupling polytope. The local construction controls one-coordinate changes for a fixed additive statistic, but reoptimizing a cut is global and nonsmooth, and individual weighting makes its oscillation depend on unequal cluster sizes. The first proof step that must change is the coordinate-sensitivity calculation for the optimized capacity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact or finite-sample conservative randomization confidence set for both endpoints, uniformly valid over fixed potential outcomes and compatible couplings, with a feasible inversion algorithm and quantified approximation when enumeration is impractical.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates randomization inference through the fragility of model-based and many-cluster CRT intervals.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CRT analyses often rely on distributional or many-cluster approximations -> randomization supplies finite-sample validity -> Pareto benefit adds coupling ambiguity and nonsmooth endpoints -> invert assignment-based tests for the whole identified interval

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt computationally efficient inversion of cluster-randomization tests for stratified designs and discrete outcomes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use active-cut directional derivatives to correct approximations when full assignment enumeration is infeasible.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The randomization statistic remains a min/max of cut scores whose local behavior changes at ties.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source construction gives a finite saddle-feasibility characterization for when common-probability independent assignment matches an unrestricted optimum, but its observation kernel and squared-error decision table concern a different endpoint. For Pareto capacities, loss is driven by estimated arm marginals and the active transport cuts, while informative cluster sizes alter orbit weights. The first changed proof step is rebuilding the kernel and risk from cluster-level cut-score laws before applying saddle and complementary-support arguments. No retrievable paper citation was available in the source artifact, so the exemplar fields remain null.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An attained finite saddle program with necessary-and-sufficient conditions for Bernoulli-design optimality and either an optimal assignment law or an explicit response-orbit witness proving a strict minimax gap.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the local minimax difficulty of deciding support-rectangle point identification for Pareto benefit when zero-width intervals meet tied-cut or vanishing-cell boundaries.

If d_n(p)=0, the entire assignment orbit has zero probability

open_problems.why_unsolved: One source supplies a common-observed-support mixture for testing lower bounds despite differing latent supports, while the other handles zero-probability faces in a finite saddle problem. Neither treats a transport interval whose width collapses only on support rectangles and whose active cut may be nonunique. The first proof step that changes is constructing local perturbations of arm marginals that preserve common observed support while opening the Pareto interval at a controlled rate. No retrievable paper citation was available in the source artifacts, so the exemplar fields remain null.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic minimax lower bound and an attaining honest test or confidence procedure for zero Pareto-capacity width, stratified by regular support rectangles, tied cuts, and vanishing marginal cells.

literature_map:
Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS) derive sharp bounds for weak and strict benefit with one ordinal outcome; their formulas rely on a total order.
Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2019, Biometrics) develop confidence intervals for the scalar fraction benefiting and identify exceptional support-based point identification.
Mullahy (2018, Journal of Health Economics; DOI 10.1016/j.jhealeco.2018.04.001) emphasizes the policy relevance of inequality probabilities such as Pr{Y(1)>Y(0)} from marginal laws.
Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory; DOI 10.1017/S0266466609990168) provide estimation and nonstandard bootstrap inference for sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds.
Strassen (1965, Annals of Mathematical Statistics) supplies the support-constrained coupling duality behind relation capacities and monotone couplings.
Yu (2020 preprint, arXiv:1912.02051) studies optimized excess-cost probabilities over couplings, but not CRT causal margins or finite-poset cut ties.
Davies Smith, Jairath, and Zou (2025, Statistical Methods in Medical Research; DOI 10.1177/09622802251338387) estimate a CRT global win probability from endpoint-specific between-patient wins.
Chen and Li (2026, arXiv:2601.13428) unify multivariate CRT causal effects, distinguish individual-pair and cluster-pair targets, address informative sizes, and derive cross-fitted efficient estimators.
Those win estimands compare different sampled patients and do not identify the same patient's cross-world strict Pareto benefit.
Wang, Park, Small, and Li (2024, JASA; DOI 10.1080/01621459.2023.2289693) establish estimand-aligned efficient CRT adjustment under variable and potentially informative sizes.
Ji, Lei, and Spector (arXiv:2310.08115) use transport duality for uniformly valid covariate-assisted inference on partially identified causal effects, but not clustered product-order endpoints.
Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies; DOI 10.1093/restud/rdy049) explain bootstrap failure for tied directionally differentiable optima and provide derivative-based resampling.
Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013, Econometrica; DOI 10.3982/ECTA8718) treat infimum and supremum envelopes as intersection bounds with bias-aware inference.
Wang, Li, and Wang (2026, Biometrics; DOI 10.1093/biomtc/ujag030) handle missing CRT outcomes and informative sizes doubly robustly for average effects, leaving joint-state Pareto transport open.
DeBar et al. (2022, Annals of Internal Medicine; DOI 10.7326/M21-1436) report PPACT's 106-cluster multivariate trial; Rabideau and Wang (2021, Biostatistics; DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxaa007) provide a finite-sample randomization-inference benchmark.
